first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding durably improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption; signup simplification also lifted SMB first-week activation. This addresses the observed funnel deterioration without relying on broad price concessions that could weaken long-term value. I would verify the underlying onboarding and pricing records before committing, because competitor pricing creates a credible alternative explanation for SMB losses and may change the experiment design.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the self-serve onboarding flow. Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, and the verified prior experiment produced +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention. This directly targets the deteriorating funnel with demonstrated downstream retention benefit. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified acquisition and qualified-revenue lift was paired with a 12% 30-day retention decline, making it unsuitable for the long-term qualified-revenue objective. Measure completion, first meaningful action, time-to-value, qualified conversion, and 30-day retention by SMB segment before rollout.
